inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: Q1 FY2027 10-Q diluted weighted-average 122.027m (basic outstanding 120.938m at 2026-09-30). Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows; no non-SBC issuance (GOJO and the Glad buyout were debt/cash funded).
inputs.sbc_source: Cash-flow statement add-back: FY2025 $81m (XBRL ShareBasedCompensation), 9M FY2026 $49m (Q3 FY2026 10-Q), Q1 FY2027 $9m; FY2026 estimated ~$70m. Clorox publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding figure and no separate net-share-settlement tax line in the files available; the add-back is used alone (small: ~1% of sales).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, staples beta ~0.65 -> cost of equity ~7.6%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.2% (BBB, post-downgrade) -> ~4.0% after tax; market-value weights ~70% equity / 30% debt (EV ~$17.3bn: market cap ~$12.2bn + net debt ~$5.0bn) -> ~6.5%, rounded up to 7.0% for the higher leverage and BBB rating. Same WACC in every scenario: risk is charged once, through the scenario paths and weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: rent sits inside operating expense and therefore inside EBITDA. Operating lease liabilities ($436m at 2026-09-30) are NOT added to net debt -- one lease treatment, no double count.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests ($160m book at 2026-09-30; ~$10-12m/yr of earnings, international subsidiaries) are deducted in the equity bridge at book. Flows are consolidated. The Glad P&G 20% interest was bought out for $476m in March 2026, so Glad is now 100% owned and no longer leaks a royalty.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route), per dcf-methods routing -- Clorox is a US branded consumer-staples operating company; no bank/REIT/holdco features. No prior DCF and no MEMORY.md entry: fresh build. US filer, USD reporting and quote, US GAAP leases -> section-7 adaptations not required beyond NCI and leases noted above. BASE REVENUE: FY2026 net sales $6,720m (FY2026 10-K Item 1 states $6.7bn; Analysis JSON / Q4 release $6.72bn; 9M FY2026 $4,772m per XBRL). Year-1 growth (+13.5%) is guidance midpoint and includes ~9.5pts from GOJO/Purell (acquired 2026-04-01, ~$2.15bn debt-funded), so the GOJO purchase price is already in net debt and its revenue enters from FY2027. DATA GAP: the FY2026 10-K text in Extracted/ carries only Items 1-1A (financial statements are incorporated by exhibit) and SEC companyfacts has no FY2026 annual values yet, so FY2026 OCF/capex/SBC are not directly verified. reported_fcf 881 is the company's FY2026 ADJUSTED free cash flow (13.1% of sales, per the Q4 FY2026 release as summarised in the Analysis JSON) -- it excludes the $476m Glad venture termination payment that depressed 9M FY2026 OCF to $282m. The forward build does not depend on it: projections are built from components off base_revenue. NET DEBT at 2026-09-30 (Q1 FY2027 10-Q): notes and loans payable (commercial paper) $1,175m + current LTD $1m + long-term debt $3,982m = $5,158m, less cash $184m = $4,974m. BUYBACKS: $256m in H1 FY2026, nil since Q3 FY2026 (deleveraging after GOJO); the flat count is therefore a modelling convention the company is not currently paying for, but SBC is only ~1% of sales so the gap is small. Dividend $4.96/yr (~$600m) is a use of owner FCF, not a deduction. Q1 FY2027 actuals (sales $1,905m +33%, diluted EPS $1.39, D&A $74m incl. GOJO intangible amortization, interest $52m) are consistent with the year-1 driver set.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Organic growth judgement (management long-term 3-5% organic algorithm, FY2027 organic guide 3.5-4.5%), NOT book value: equity CAGR is meaningless for Clorox.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-13% / -16%) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue and EPS CAGRs. Book value is near zero or negative (Clorox stockholders' equity -$39m at 2026-09-30; total equity $252m at FY2026) after decades of buybacks and the debt-funded GOJO deal, so the house default of selecting equity CAGR is not usable. EPS 3yr CAGR (+58.5%) is distorted by the FY2023 trough ($1.21, cyberattack + impairments).
historical_growth.notes: Endpoints: revenue FY2023 $7,389m / FY2021 $7,341m -> FY2026 $6,720m (FY2021 was COVID-inflated; FY2025 had ERP pull-forward; FY2026 the offsetting drawdown and the VMS divestiture). EPS FY2023 $1.21 / FY2021 $5.66 -> FY2026 $4.81. Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC): FY2021 $895m, FY2023 $857m, FY2026 ~$811m (adjusted basis). Owner-FCF and reported-FCF CAGRs are close because SBC is small (~1% of sales) and stable -- SBC is not growing faster than cash flow.

base.growth_rates_note: Y1 = FY2027 guidance midpoint (+13-14% incl. ~9.5pts GOJO; organic 3.5-4.5%). Then ~3% organic (mid of management's 3-5% algorithm, haircut for mature US categories) fading to 2.5%.
base.ebitda_margin_path_note: Pre-SBC EBITDA. FY2027 guide (adj EPS $5.70-6.00, ~42% gross margin, >$200m inflation) back-solves to ~20% after interest ~$205m and D&A ~$300m; Q1 FY2027 ran ~18% in the seasonally weak quarter. Recovery to 21% as ERP costs end, GOJO synergies land and gross margin rebuilds toward the 43-44% of FY2019 -- not to the COVID peak.
base.da_pct_path_note: Q1 FY2027 D&A $74m (x4 ~ $300m, ~3.9% of guided sales) includes GOJO intangible amortization; drifts to 3.5% as the ERP asset amortizes out.
base.capex_pct_path_note: History 3.0-4.5% of sales (FY2021 peak 4.5% during ERP/capacity build; FY2025 3.1%). 3.5% carries GOJO's dispenser/plant capex.
base.cash_tax_rate_path_note: Clorox's normal effective rate ~23-25% (FY2025 GAAP 23.6%; cash taxes $264m). No NOL or valuation-allowance distortion to ramp.
base.wc_capture_pct_note: Manufacturer: growth consumes working capital (negative capture), muted by the supplier-finance programme.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 lands at the guidance midpoint: GOJO adds ~9.5 points and organic sales grow ~4% against the easy ERP-drawdown comparison, but >$200m of resin, chemical and freight inflation holds gross margin near 42%. From FY2028 Clorox returns to a ~3% organic algorithm in mature US categories, with Purell's ~20m-dispenser installed base providing steadier B2B refill revenue. EBITDA margin rebuilds to ~21% (FY2019-like, not the COVID peak) as ERP implementation costs roll off and GOJO integration synergies land. Leverage (~3.3x) is worked down from cash flow with buybacks paused; the new CEO (Fabian Garcia, January 2027) executes IGNITE without a strategic reset.
scenario_narratives.bull: Purell proves the structural margin lever management claims: institutional/healthcare refills grow mid-single digit, cross-selling through CloroxPro widens the B2B channel, and full Glad ownership (no P&G royalty) plus a stabilized ERP lift gross margin back toward 44-45%. Organic growth runs 4-4.5% for three years on IGNITE innovation (Clorox PURE, Fresh Step Lightweight, Glad MaxStrength) as consumers stop trading down. EBITDA margin reaches ~23% and the market keeps paying a premium-staple 20x exit for the cash flow.
scenario_narratives.bear: Private-label trade-down persists and Walmart (~26% of sales) and the other top-five customers press on price and shelf space; organic growth stalls near 1% for two years. Inflation above the historical $75-100m range recurs, the gross margin stays around 41-42% and GOJO integration stumbles under a CEO change, so EBITDA margin settles at ~18.5% -- below FY2025. With equity negative and the rating at BBB, a further downgrade raises funding cost and forces the dividend to absorb most of the FCF. The exit multiple compresses to 15x for a low-growth, levered staple.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: leverage has doubled (net debt ~$5.0bn, S&P cut to BBB, negative Clorox equity), the CEO changes mid-integration, and >$200m inflation plus private-label pressure is already in the FY2027 guide. Base 50%: guidance has just been reaffirmed and Q1 FY2027 came in ahead of the flagged weak-Q1 shape. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs GOJO margin accretion, gross-margin recovery and a consumer turn to all go right together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Clorox is a mature, cash-generative branded staple whose value is a ~3% growing stream of ~11-13% owner-FCF margins. The equity is a levered claim after the debt-funded GOJO deal: ~$5.0bn of net debt sits ahead of a ~$12bn market cap, so modest changes in the margin path move per-share value materially. SBC is small (~1% of sales), so the house and street bases sit close together.
key_risks_to_valuation: EBITDA-margin recovery to ~21% depends on gross margin rebuilding from ~42% while FY2027 inflation exceeds $200m
GOJO/Purell integration and its claimed margin accretion under a new CEO
Leverage: net debt ~$5.0bn, BBB rating; a further downgrade raises funding cost and collateral calls
Walmart ~26% and top-five customers ~50% of sales: retailer pricing and private-label pressure
FY2026 annual cash-flow statement not in the extracted files: base FCF is the company's adjusted figure, not independently verified
Terminal value is capped at 18x (base) FCF; value is terminal-heavy, as for any mature staple
